questions.prompt: Which statement is the correct definition of f(n) = O(g(n))?

options.text: There exist positive c and n₀ with 0 ≤ f(n) ≤ c·g(n) for all n ≥ n₀
There exist positive c and n₀ with 0 ≤ c·g(n) ≤ f(n) for all n ≥ n₀
f(n) equals g(n) for every n
f(n) is smaller than g(n) for at least one value of n

questions.explanation: Big-O is an asymptotic upper bound: f is eventually bounded above by a constant multiple of g. Option (b) is the definition of Ω.

questions.prompt: What is the tight (Θ) bound for 3n² + 100n + 7?
questions.explanation: Drop the constant factor (3) and the lower-order terms (100n, 7); the fastest-growing term is n², so the tight bound is Θ(n²).

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: If f(n) = Θ(g(n)) then f(n) = O(g(n))
For large enough n, 2ⁿ exceeds n¹⁰⁰
Worst-case time is an upper-bound guarantee on running time
An O(n²) algorithm is always slower than an O(n) algorithm for every input size

questions.explanation: Θ implies O; exponential eventually beats any polynomial; worst case is a guarantee. But for small n, constant factors can let an O(n²) routine beat an O(n) one, so (d) is false.

questions.prompt: The worst-case time of linear search over n elements is O(____). (fill the growth term)
questions.explanation: In the worst case the target is absent or last, so all n elements are compared: O(n).

questions.prompt: Order these growth classes from slowest-growing to fastest-growing.
questions.explanation: The standard ladder: 1 < log n < n < n log n < n² < 2ⁿ.

questions.prompt: Match each code pattern with its typical time complexity.

pairs.left: Two nested loops over n items

questions.explanation: Indexing is constant; one pass is linear; a nested pass is quadratic; halving each step is logarithmic.
